## Gates

- From the repository root, run `just check` (`check-hygiene`: ops-check, ops-docs check, the document link and anchor check (`python/tools/check_doc_links.py`), `tasks check`; then `check-code`: ruff check, ruff format --check, pyright, tsc, biome) and `just test` (the parallel Python suite, then the TypeScript suite). `just gate` runs both. Every check and suite runs through the vendored timing wrapper `tools/tt`, so every run is recorded (ops `docs/tooling.md`); `check` and `gate` are untimed compositions whose children record their own rows. Formatting covers every Python file; `.git-blame-ignore-revs` lists both reformats.
- Test execution policy comes from `.tt.toml` at the Git top level, validated by `tools/tt` (ops `docs/test-execution-policy.md`; adoption: beliefs's test-execution-policy design of 2026-10-31, kept with its records). If the file is absent, policy is enabled and every target runs. With `automatic_broad = false`, the broad targets it lists (`test`, `test-fast`, `test-push`, `check-code`, `ci-python`, `ci-typescript`) are recorded as skipped instead of run, unless `TT_FORCE=1` is set; `test-one`, `test-full`, `check-hygiene`, `setup` and the hooks are protected and always run. A skip is a decision, never a pass or a timing sample. This checkout's `.tt.toml` sets `automatic_broad = false`, so those broad targets skip locally and hosted CI carries them on every branch push.
- Focused Python runs: `just test-one tests/test_file.py`, `just test-one tests/test_file.py::test_name`, or `just test-one -k "a and b"` (paths relative to `python/`). Focused TypeScript runs: `just --set one_cmd "cd ts && npx --no-install vitest run" test-one <filename-filter> -t "<test-name>"` (filters relative to `ts/`). Arguments reach the runner intact; at least one is required. The recipe runs under `host-budget run`. `just setup` installs the TypeScript dependencies (`npm ci`, which is installation, not a gate); the Python side needs none, since `uv run --frozen` builds the locked environment on first use.
- `just test-fast` runs all Python tests in parallel plus the affected TypeScript tests. The Python phase uses `loadgroup`: module/class fixture consumers share file/class groups, while other tests schedule separately. The push hook treats a push to `origin` whose every ref matches `ci_suite_refs` (now `refs/heads/*`, every branch) as covered by CI's complete package suites; any other push (another remote, or a tag) takes the full local route, whose suite policy skips with a warning. Hand-run full suites are costly here.
- Deliberate verification: `just test-full` forces `test` and is suite evidence, its forced `test` row; it runs no hygiene, lint or typecheck. `TT_FORCE=1 just gate` is full-gate evidence: the consecutive `check-hygiene`, `check-code` and `test` rows of one invocation, with the same `rev`, `dirty` and `content`, each `execution: ran`. Unforced rows under enabled policy are equally valid; under policy-off the broad rows need `TT_FORCE=1`. Evidence cited for a change names which of the two it is. A policy skip or a hook completion is never evidence that a suite or gate passed.
- The git hooks in `.githooks/` run `just hook-pre-commit` at pre-commit: hygiene, timed under the hook's target, then `just check-code`. Only commits whose every staged path matches the justfile's `docs_paths` run `just hook-pre-commit-docs` instead (hygiene only, well under a second); renames count on both sides and failed classification runs the full check. At pre-push, `just hook-pre-push-fast` runs hygiene, `just check-code` and `just test-push` (all Python tests and the full TypeScript suite) when CI covers every pushed ref on `origin`; `just hook-pre-push` runs hygiene, `just check-code` and `just test` otherwise, and warns when policy skips that suite with no remote coverage declared. Since this split, hook targets time hygiene only, `check` is untimed, and `check-hygiene`, `check-code` and `test-push` are new series; none is compared with the earlier whole-hook or `check` medians. On a fresh clone run `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` once.
- Remote CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `just ci-python` (Python 3.11 and 3.13) and `just ci-typescript` (Node 20 and 24) on every branch push, on manual dispatch, and on fork pull requests (a same-repository PR's branch push already ran). A newer push to a ref cancels the older run, which leaves that revision unverified. The jobs set `TT_FORCE=1`, so tt policy never skips them, and upload JUnit plus a module inventory (with the atoms and nodes revisions) as 30-day artifacts. It runs the recipes rather than `just gate` because the `tasks` binary is not on a runner. It costs nothing: verifiably/beliefs is public, and standard GitHub-hosted runners are free in public repositories on every plan, drawing on no private-repo minute allowance. Larger, GPU and macOS runners are billed even on public repos, so CI stays on standard Linux.
- `CapabilityUnavailable` is a fail-closed result, not a waiver: on the certified kernel and volume tuple the suite runs closed and that exception is a failure. CI sets `VERIFIABLY_UNCERTIFIED_HOST=1`, which converts *only* that exception into a skip whose message starts `certified tuple unavailable on this host:`; every other failure still fails, and only an explicit `1` disarms anything. A green CI is therefore evidence about the portable tests and never about the capability-dependent ones — those are proven only by a run on the certified tuple. Under policy-off no routine local route runs them, so a change that touches capability-dependent behaviour (the `root.py` atoms boundary, durability, publication persistence) runs the affected tests with `just test-one` on the certified tuple, chosen by test ID from the latest hosted artifact's capability-skip list; `TT_FORCE=1 just test-fast` sweeps every capability test outside `python/tests/acceptance/` (about 90 s) when a change's reach is unclear, and `just test-acceptance` runs the acceptance modules. If such a run hits `CapabilityUnavailable` here, the host is off the certified tuple: report the exact mismatch.
- Acceptance: `python/tests/acceptance/` is excluded from every other recipe (`addopts` ignores it); `just test-acceptance` runs every module in its own process, from beside the main checkout on the certified volume (about 25 min). It errors and never skips: exit 2 when its probe is refused (off the certified tuple), 3 when an old `SCIENCE_CUT<n>_ROOT` variable is set, 4 when no modules are found, 5 when any argument is given (the recipe takes none: a focused run is `just test-one tests/acceptance/<module>.py`). Those meanings hold only before any module runs: once the probe passes, a non-zero exit is the failing module's own pytest code (pytest also uses 2 for an interrupted run or collection error and 4 for a usage error), and the message tells the cases apart. It is not a broad target, so tt policy never skips it. Work roots: `BELIEFS_ACCEPTANCE_ROOT` (default .work/acceptance beside the main checkout) and, for the ordinary suite's real-engine fixtures, `BELIEFS_TEST_ROOT` (default .work/tests, likewise). `docs/development.md` covers both, and `just mm30-recreate WORK PREDECESSOR`.

## Layout

- `python/`, `ts/`, `fixtures/`, `contracts/`, `domains/`, `tools/` — as the README's Layout.
- `docs/` — the public documents: `guide.md`, `development.md`, `glossary.md`, and the
  reference documents `records.md`, `contracts.md` and `writes.md`. Task records, design specs, plans and every other working document live
  in beliefs's records directory, committed in the records repository.

## Rules

- The reference documents specify what the code must do: the two the Authority line names, and `docs/contracts.md` for contract documents. Change a reference, and any guide that describes the same behaviour, in the same change that alters that behaviour. Every public document states only what the code at its revision does.
- Verify status and checklist claims against code, tests, history, branches, and worktrees.
- New design specs, plans, briefs and handoffs go to beliefs's records directory (its specs, plans and notes directories), committed in the records repository; public documents never link into them.

Two architecture rules are tested; carry both into every plan that touches the kernel.

- **`root.py` is the one `atoms` importer** (`test_capability_boundary.py`,
  `TestTheCompositionRootIsTheOneAtomsImporter`). A classification over engine
  cause types, a predicate over engine exceptions, or any other engine-typed
  behaviour lives in `root.py` and reaches its boundary through a seam callable
  (such as `StoreActSeam.store_refusal`), never as an import in the boundary module.
- **Every caller of a write primitive is inventoried.** It joins
  `WRITE_ENTRY_POINTS` in `test_permit_boundary.py` and gains a `Case` in
  `test_permit_entry_points.py`'s `CASES`; the inventory is closed in both
  directions.
